agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

    UsingDirective(UsingDirective),
    UserDefinedValueType(UserDefinedValueType),
    ConstructorDefinition(FunctionDefinition),
    FallbackDefinition(FunctionDefinition),
    ReceiveDefinition(FunctionDefinition),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FunctionDefinition {
    pub kind: FunctionKind,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub params: Vec<Parameter>,
    pub return_params: Vec<Parameter>,
    pub visibility: Visibility,
    pub mutability: Mutability,
    pub modifiers: Vec<String>,
    pub is_virtual: bool,
    pub is_override: bool,
    pub body: Option<()>, // just track if body exists
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum FunctionKind {
    Function,
    Constructor,
    Fallback,
    Receive,
    Modifier,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Parameter {
    pub type_: TypeName,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub data_location: Option<DataLocation>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum TypeName {
    Elementary(ElementaryType),
    Array(Box<TypeName>, Option<Box<Expression>>),
    Mapping(Box<TypeName>, Box<TypeName>),
    UserDefined(Vec<String>), // path like ["MyContract", "MyStruct"]
    Function(Vec<TypeName>, Vec<TypeName>),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElementaryType {
    Address(bool), // bool = payable
    Bool,
    String,
    Bytes, // bytes (dynamic)
    FixedBytes(u8), // bytes1..bytes32
    Int(u8), // bits / 8, 0 means 256
    Uint(u8),
    Fixed(u8, u8),
    Ufixed(u8, u8),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum DataLocation {
    Storage,
    Memory,
    Calldata,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Visibility {
    Public,
    External,
    Internal,
    Private,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Mutability {
    Pure,
    View,
    Payable,
    NonPayable,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StateVariableDeclaration {
    pub type_: TypeName,
    pub visibility: Visibility,
    pub name: String,
    pub value: Option<()>,
    pub is_constant: bool,
    pub is_immutable: bool,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EventDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Vec<EventParameter>,
    pub anonymous: bool,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EventParameter {
    pub type_: TypeName,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub indexed: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ErrorDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Vec<Parameter>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StructDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub fields: Vec<StructField>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StructField {
    pub type_: TypeName,
    pub name: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EnumDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub values: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct UserDefinedValueType {
    pub name: String,
    pub underlying: ElementaryType,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ModifierDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Vec<Parameter>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct UsingDirective {
    pub library: Vec<String>,
    pub type_: Option<TypeName>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expression {
    Literal(String),
    Identifier(String),
    BinaryOp(Box<Expression>, String, Box<Expression>),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct Span {
    pub start: usize,
    pub end: usize,
}

    fn parse_state_variable_declaration(&mut self) -> Result<StateVariableDeclaration, ParseError> {

pub fn emit_analysis_error(
    err: &AnalysisError,
    format: &str,
    style: &str,
    use_color: bool,
    diagnostic_width: Option<usize>,
) {
    let (line, col) = offset_to_line_col(&err.content, err.span.start);
    let span_len = if err.span.end > err.span.start { err.span.end - err.span.start } else { 1 };
    let line_text = get_line(&err.content, line);
    
    // Build secondary spans
    let mut secondaries = Vec::new();
    for note in &err.notes {
        secondaries.push(note.clone());
    }
    
    match format {
        "json" => {
            let human_msg = format_human_error(
                &err.message, err.code.as_deref(), &err.file, line, col, span_len, &line_text, style, use_color,
                None, &err.notes, None
            );
            let formatted_escaped = escape_json(&human_msg);
            let msg_escaped = escape_json(&err.message);
            let src_loc = if err.file.is_empty() {
                "null".to_string()
            } else {
                format!("{{\"file\":\"{}\",\"start\":{},\"end\":{}}}", 
                    escape_json(&err.file), err.span.start, err.span.end)
            };
            eprintln!("{{\"sourceLocation\":{},\"secondarySourceLocations\":[],\"type\":\"Exception\",\"component\":\"general\",\"severity\":\"{}\",\"errorCode\":null,\"message\":\"{}\",\"formattedMessage\":\"{}\"}}",
                src_loc, err.severity, msg_escaped, formatted_escaped);
        }
        "rustc-json" => {
            let human_msg = format_human_error(
                &err.message, err.code.as_deref(), &err.file, line, col, span_len, &line_text, style, false,
                None, &err.notes, None
            );
            let formatted_escaped = escape_json(&human_msg);
            let msg_escaped = escape_json(&err.message);
            eprintln!("{{\"$message_type\":\"diagnostic\",\"message\":\"{}\",\"code\":null,\"level\":\"{}\",\"spans\":[],\"children\":[],\"rendered\":\"{}\"}}",
                msg_escaped, err.severity, formatted_escaped);
        }
        _ => {
            let human_msg = format_human_error(
                &err.message, err.code.as_deref(), &err.file, line, col, span_len, &line_text, style, use_color,
                None, &err.notes, None
            );
            eprint!("{}", human_msg);
        }
    }
}

# Final comprehensive test - run all the earlier examples from my exploration
cat > /tmp/test_all.sh << 'TESTS_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
ORIG="./executable"
NEW="/tmp/fresh_checkout/executable"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

run_test() {
    local name="$1"
    local sol_code="$2"
    local extra_args="${3:-}"
    
    diff <(echo "$sol_code" | $ORIG - $extra_args 2>&1) \
         <(echo "$sol_code" | $NEW - $extra_args 2>&1) > /dev/null 2>&1
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS+1))
    else
        echo "FAIL: $name"
        echo "Expected:"
        echo "$sol_code" | $ORIG - $extra_args 2>&1 | head -10
        echo "Got:"
        echo "$sol_code" | $NEW - $extra_args 2>&1 | head -10
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
    fi
}

# All the test cases
run_test "basic_empty" "contract C {}" "--emit abi"
run_test "basic_function" "contract C { function foo() public pure returns (uint) { return 42; } }" "--emit abi"
run_test "basic_pretty" "contract C { function foo() public pure returns (uint) { return 42; } }" "--emit abi --pretty-json"
run_test "basic_hash" "contract C { function foo() public pure returns (uint) { return 42; } }" "--emit hashes"

# Statmutability
run_test "pure_func" "contract C { function foo() public pure returns (uint) {} }" "--emit abi"
run_test "view_func" "contract C { function foo() public view returns (uint) {} }" "--emit abi"
run_test "payable_func" "contract C { function foo() public payable {} }" "--emit abi"
run_test "nonpayable_func" "contract C { function foo() public {} }" "--emit abi"

# Constructor
run_test "constructor" "contract C { constructor(uint x) {} }" "--emit abi"
run_test "payable_constructor" "contract C { constructor() payable {} }" "--emit abi"

# Events and errors
run_test "event" "contract C { event MyEvent(uint x, address indexed y); }" "--emit abi"
run_test "error" "contract C { error MyError(uint x); }" "--emit abi"
run_test "anon_event" "contract C { event MyEvent(uint x) anonymous; }" "--emit abi"

# State variables
run_test "public_var" "contract C { uint public x; }" "--emit abi"
run_test "mapping_var" "contract C { mapping(address => uint) public balances; }" "--emit abi"
run_test "nested_mapping" "contract C { mapping(address => mapping(address => uint)) public allowance; }" "--emit abi"

# Fallback/receive
run_test "fallback" "contract C { fallback() external {} }" "--emit abi"
run_test "receive" "contract C { receive() external payable {} }" "--emit abi"

# Errors
run_test "parse_error" "contract C { invalid }" ""
run_test "no_visibility" "contract C { function foo() { } }" ""

# Multiple contracts
